problems.title: Odd-period shifts fail to invert
problems.source_location: Section 3.3, Eq.(7), PDF p.6; Table 7, p.28; SGN.py, TemporalSwinTransformerBlock.forward, lines 164–191
claim: The right cyclic shift is said to restore the original coordinates after shifting by \(P/2\). The release uses floor-divided shifts \((-P)//2\) and \(P//2\); the PTB-XL configuration has \(P=25\).
analysis: For \(P=2k+1\), the shifts sum to \(-(k+1)+k=-1\), rather than zero. With an identity feature map, \(P=3\) and input \((0,1,2,3,4,5)\), the two rolls give \((1,2,3,4,5,0)\); the prefix overwrite yields \((0,2,3,4,5,0)\). Even periods give cancelling shifts.
result: The released odd-period coordinate mapping does not implement the stated restoration. This does not establish any change in benchmark accuracy.
repair: Compute \(h=\lfloor P/2\rfloor\) once and use shifts \(-h,+h\); their cyclic maps are inverse for every integer period.
problems.impact_rationale: The odd-period coordinate mapping is wrong in the release; no effect on the central classification gains is established.
problems.existing_correction_status: The described correction remains a proposal; author adoption or a corresponding erratum is not established.

problems.title: Initialization always loads TDBRAIN assignments
problems.source_location: Section 3.1, PDF p.4; Appendix A, p.24; SGN.py, GumbelGroupEmbedding.__init__, line 237; exp_classification.py, _build_model, lines 44–67
claim: The model initializes grouping from the selected dataset, but the embedding always reads groups_matrix_T.npy.
analysis: The builder writes distinct files for TDBRAIN, PTB-XL, FLAAP and UCI-HAR, with shapes \[(33,4),(12,4),(6,5),(9,6)\]. A clean PTB-XL build writes only its own file, so the fixed TDBRAIN filename is absent. If the TDBRAIN file exists instead, its \(33\) channel rows cannot contract with the \(12\) PTB-XL input channels.
result: The published construction path has a concrete filename/shape mismatch. An unpublished renaming workflow and the experimental snapshot remain unknown.
repair: Pass the selected assignment matrix directly to the embedding and require its shape to equal \((C,G)\).
problems.impact_rationale: This is a reproducibility failure in the released dataset-to-initializer interface, with the experimental snapshot unknown.
problems.existing_correction_status: The described correction remains a proposal; author adoption or a corresponding erratum is not established.

problems.title: Cosine regularization changes assignment preferences
problems.source_location: Section 3.1, Eq.(3), PDF p.5; SGN.py, similarity_regularization, lines 276–280
claim: The paper uses \(L=\sum_{ij}S_{ij}\|M_i-M_j\|^2\), with signed cosine similarities. The release uses weights \((1+S_{ij})/2\) and divides by \(C^2\).
analysis: For \(C=G=2\), assignment rows \((1,0),(0,1)\), and off-diagonal cosine \(s\), the paper gives \(4s\) while the release gives \((1+s)/2\). At \(s=-1\), these are \(-4\) and \(0\); at \(s=0\), they are \(0\) and \(1/2\). The difference includes an unweighted pair-distance penalty and cannot be absorbed into a positive loss rescaling.
result: The documented and released objectives are inequivalent, including interior soft assignments by continuity. Which objective generated the tables is not established.
repair: Specify whether signed cosine weights or shifted nonnegative weights are intended, and align the displayed objective and implementation.
problems.impact_rationale: The two assignment objectives can prefer different groupings, but the training objective behind the published results is not identified.
problems.existing_correction_status: The described correction remains a proposal; author adoption or a corresponding erratum is not established.

problems.title: Initializer computes squared distance correlation
problems.source_location: Appendix A, Eqs.(9)–(12), PDF p.24; exp_classification.py, distance covariance and similarity functions
claim: The paper clusters rows of distance correlation \(R_n\); the routine returns squared distance covariance and therefore normalizes to \(R_n^2\).
analysis: For \(X=(0,1,2,3)^\top\) and \(Y=(0,1,0,1)^\top\), double-centering gives cross-value \(1/8\) and self-values \(13/16,1/4\). Thus the routine returns \(R_n^2=1/\sqrt{13}\), whereas Eq.(9) gives \(R_n=13^{-1/4}\). Entrywise squaring is nonlinear, so it need not preserve Euclidean row distances used by K-means.
result: The formula/routine discrepancy is established for nonconstant samples. The builder loads precomputed matrices, so this does not determine their provenance or show that the benchmark groupings change.
repair: Take the nonnegative square root of the normalized squared quantity to match Eq.(9), with an explicit zero-variance convention; alternatively document the squared initializer.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a local formula/routine mismatch; precomputed benchmark matrices are not shown to use the routine.
problems.existing_correction_status: The described correction remains a proposal; author adoption or a corresponding erratum is not established.

problems.title: FLAAP loader does not enforce subject separation
problems.source_location: Section 4.1, PDF pp.7–8; Appendix B.3, p.25; data_loader.py, FLAAPLoader.load_flaap_dependent, lines 622–648
claim: The experiment description restricts each subject to one data subset. The released FLAAP loader splits sample arrays twice without receiving subject identifiers.
analysis: The function calls sample-level train_test_split with test fractions \(0.2\) and \(0.25\), producing \(60/20/20\) sample proportions. Subject labels do not enter either call. Therefore windows from the same subject are eligible for different subsets; sample partitioning alone cannot establish the stated subject-disjoint guarantee. TDBRAIN instead uses explicit identifier lists.
result: The release lacks the claimed safeguard. Actual FLAAP subject overlap and score inflation require the unavailable benchmark split manifest; neither is established by this source check.
repair: Partition by subject identifiers and publish the disjoint subject lists, allowing approximate sample proportions when subject sizes differ.
problems.impact_rationale: The release lacks a subject safeguard, but actual benchmark subject overlap and performance inflation remain unproven.
problems.existing_correction_status: The described correction remains a proposal; author adoption or a corresponding erratum is not established.
